newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-CAGE RECORDS FIRST TOUR VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-CAGE RECORDS FIRST TOUR VICTORY.

text.p: Stuart Cage became the fourth first-time winner on the European Tour this season with a five-stroke victory in the Cannes Open at Royal Mougins on Sunday.

After taking the lead by the 16th in the second round, Cage never allowed himself to be headed and collected the 50,000 pounds ($81,600) first prize and equivalent Ryder Cup points with a determined display.
A final-round 66 left the Yorkshireman on 14-under 270, five shots better than compatriot Paul Broadhurst, who had been within a stroke of the lead by the turn, and David Carter.
Carter's closing round 62 did not officially equal the course record 62 he shot last year as preferred lies were in use because of soaked fairways.
But his finish was a remarkable achievement bearing in mind that less than two months ago he was undergoing emergency surgery in Dubai to relieve fluid on the brain.

Carter's finale, though, was not the lowest of the day. Another Englishman, Jamie Spence -- joint holder of the European 72-hole record 60 -- posted a 61 to share fourth place on eight under with compatriot Paul Eales, whose bogey at the last for a 69, playing alongside Cage, denied him a share of the runners-up spot.
Cage showed his nerve in the closing round by fending off Broadhurst. Having been four in front by the sixth, Cage was pegged back to just one ahead by the ninth.
But he got out of trouble with a couple of birdies and then posted two more at the 15th and 16th to shut out the challengers.
"I was so wrapped up in what I was doing I hardly had time to be nervous," he said afterwards.
"I just kept pounding away. It wasn't until the final two holes after I'd birdied the 15th and 16th, that I got really nervous and almost lost concentration.

"It's a big breakthrough...When I won the English Amateur I thought that was the best thing I'd ever done, then when I won on the Challenge Tour it was the best and now I know that the guys who I thought were unbeatable on the European Tour can be beaten."
Cage also compiled scores in the 60s for four rounds for the first time in his career.
